full_text_en:
Qingdao Huaren Property Co., Ltd. v. Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd., Qingdao Branch, et al. — dispute over property service contract

Ruling Summary

1. Where an individual property owner and the construction unit agree in the sale and purchase contract for the commercial housing to exclude the content of the preliminary property service contract, such agreement is not effective against the property service enterprise, and the property owner shall still be bound by the preliminary property service contract.

2. In determining the property fee under the preliminary property service contract relationship, full consideration shall be given to the differences between the preliminary property service contract and the property service contract in terms of the parties signing the contract, the competitiveness and openness of price negotiation, public perception, owner acceptance, and contract termination. Where no opportunity was given to an individual property owner or the owners' group to participate in the negotiation of the preliminary property service contract, strictly applying the unit price stated in the contract may lead to an imbalance of interests. The calculation of the property fee shall be based on the amount determined in accordance with the fee standard in the preliminary property service contract, and shall be comprehensively determined in light of the actual circumstances.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2022) Supreme People's Court Civil Retrial No. 223

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Qingdao Huaren Property Co., Ltd., domiciled at Rooms 3137 and 3136-2, No. 37 Donghai West Road, Shinan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Xie Yanyan, Chairperson of the Company.

Agent Ad Litem: Zhao Zhonghua, lawyer at Beijing Yinghe Law Firm.

Agent Ad Litem: Zhuang Yucong, lawyer at Beijing Yinghe Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd., Qingdao Branch, domiciled at No. 29 Donghai West Road, Shinan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Person in Charge: Hou Chuanhe, Branch Manager.

Agent Ad Litem: Wang Xiaoming, lawyer at Beijing Chuting Law Firm.

Agent Ad Litem: Zhao Wen, lawyer at Beijing Chuting Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Qingdao Haiyi Tiancheng Commercial Management Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 1103, Unit 3, Building 3, No. 63 Hong Kong Middle Road, Shinan District, Qingdao, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: An Ming, Executive Director and General Manager of the Company.

The applicant for retrial, Qingdao Huaren Property Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huaren Property Company), filed an application with this Court for retrial of the civil judgment (2020) Lu Civil Final No. 2866 rendered by the Shandong High People's Court in a dispute over property service contract with respondents Hengfeng Bank Co., Ltd., Qingdao Branch (hereinafter referred to as Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch) and Qingdao Haiyi Tiancheng Commercial Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haiyi Company). This Court issued a civil ruling (2021) Supreme People's Court Civil Application No. 6280 on March 15, 2022, granting the retrial. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a hearing. Zhao Zhonghua and Zhuang Yucong, agents ad litem of Huaren Property Company, and Wang Xiaoming and Zhao Wen, agents ad litem of Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch, appeared before the court to participate in the proceedings. Respondent Haiyi Company only submitted a written defense and did not appear before the court after being summoned by summons. This Court conducted the trial by default in accordance with the law. The trial of this case is now concluded.

Huaren Property Company applied for retrial on the grounds that: Huaren Property Company applied for retrial pursuant to Items 1, 2, and 6 of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, requesting: 1. To set aside the civil judgment (2020) Lu Civil Final No. 2866 of the Shandong High People's Court and the civil judgment (2019) Lu 71 Civil First Instance No. 87 of the Jinan Railway Transport Intermediate Court; 2. To ascertain the facts and amend the judgment to support all of Huaren Property Company's claims; 3. To order Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company to bear all litigation costs of this case. Facts and reasons: (1) The first and second instance judgments erroneously applied the law. a. Huaren Property Company was selected through lawful procedures, and the Haiyi Tiancheng Preliminary Property Service Contract (hereinafter referred to as the Preliminary Property Service Contract) was filed with the competent authority, making it a legally valid property service contract. b. Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company expressly agreed that Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch should pay water, electricity, property fees, and related expenses on time. Pursuant to Article 7 of the former Judicial Interpretation on Specific Issues Concerning the Trial of Property Service Dispute Cases (hereinafter referred to as the Property Service Judicial Interpretation), both respondents are obligated to pay property service fees. c. The first and second instance courts failed to apply the Property Service Judicial Interpretation, which is erroneous. Article 1 of that interpretation provides that a preliminary property service contract lawfully concluded by the construction unit with a property service enterprise is binding on the property owners, and a property owner's defense that he is not a party to the contract shall not be upheld by the people's court. d. Huaren Property Company has submitted evidence to prove that the Preliminary Property Service Contract is legally valid. The first and second instance courts required Huaren Property Company to prove that the Preliminary Property Service Contract is binding on Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company. This allocation of the burden of proof is erroneous and unreasonably increases Huaren Property Company's burden. Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company failed to provide valid evidence to deny the existence of the preliminary property service contract relationship and should bear the consequences of their failure to adduce evidence. (2) The basic facts found by the first and second instance courts lacked evidentiary support. a. The properties purchased by Haiyi Company are not a single unit but 52 separate houses with planned uses of catering, accommodation, and urban residential use, each having its own real estate registration. These houses are no different from other units in the Haiyi Tiancheng project and together constitute a complete property management area. The first and second instance courts failed to clearly find this fact. b. In the 52 Qingdao Commercial Housing Pre-sale Contracts entered into between Haiyi Company and Huanhai Company, Article 11 of the Supplementary Agreement expressly states that Haiyi Company agrees that Huanhai Company designates Huaren Property Company to provide management services for areas other than those purchased by Haiyi Company. Haiyi Company has expressly accepted Huaren Property Company's property services, but only requested self-management within the purchased area. The contract does not exclude Huaren Property Company's management of the common areas of the Haiyi Tiancheng project. The first and second instance courts failed to clearly find this fact. c. The provisions in the Supplementary Agreement to the said Qingdao Commercial Housing Pre-sale Contracts that exclude the effect of the Preliminary Property Service Contract infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of the property service provider and other property owners of the Haiyi Tiancheng project and should be null and void as a matter of law. d. The scope of property services provided by Huaren Property Company pertains to the common parts and common facilities and equipment of the Haiyi Tiancheng project, and does not include the office area of Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch. Security, cleaning, and maintenance of common facilities and equipment in the common areas of the Haiyi Tiancheng project have always been the responsibility of Huaren Property Company. Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company have enjoyed the property services provided by Huaren Property Company. The first and second instance courts failed to clearly find this fact. The fundamental reason why the Preliminary Property Service Contract could not be fully performed was that Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch refused Huaren Property Company's provision of property services in the common parts of the closed Haiyi Tiancheng project. Huaren Property Company has the right to demand continued performance of the contract. (3) There is new evidence sufficient to overturn the original judgment. Huaren Property Company commissioned Beijing Zhankang Property Service Appraisal and Supervision Co., Ltd. to appraise the preliminary property service fees for the Haiyi Tiancheng project, proving that the amount determined by the original trial court at its discretion lacked factual basis.

Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch argued: (1) Haiyi Company and the developer had agreed in the Qingdao Commercial Housing Pre-sale Contracts to exclude Huaren Property Company's provision of property services in the area purchased by Haiyi Company. Huaren Property Company also demonstrated through its actual conduct that it had agreed to allow Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch to manage the property on its own. Therefore, Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch should not pay property service fees to Huaren Property Company. a. Article 11 of the Supplementary Agreement in issue expressly modifies the Preliminary Property Service Contract, excluding Huaren Property Company from providing property services in the area purchased by Haiyi Company. Therefore, Haiyi Company and Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch, as lessees, are not bound by the Preliminary Property Service Contract. b. Huaren Property Company and Huanhai Company did not conduct property inspection and handover of the common parts and common equipment and facilities in the area in question. Huaren Property Company has known from the beginning that it is not required to provide property services in that area. c. From the time Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch moved in until before January 2019, Huaren Property Company never claimed property fees from Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch and never raised any objection to Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch's entrustment of a third-party professional unit for management. Huaren Property Company has demonstrated through its actual conduct that it agreed to allow Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch to manage the property in the area in question on its own. d. Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch's entrustment of a third party to manage the area in question is based on special regulatory requirements for business premises of banking financial institutions, and is not a deliberate refusal of Huaren Property Company's property management services. (2) Even if the Preliminary Property Service Contract is considered binding on Haiyi Company and Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch, because Huaren Property Company only provided partial property services in fact, the original trial judgment's discretionary determination of the property service fee based on the actual property services provided by Huaren Property Company is entirely correct and fair, and should be affirmed. a. Haiyi Company is the sole owner of the podium (excluding the sixth-floor clubhouse) in question. Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch's closure of the area and entrustment of a third party for property management did not affect other property owners' use of the common parts and common facilities, nor did it infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of other property owners. The installation of turnstiles or access controls is not a construction activity and does not require approval from the relevant construction authorities. b. Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch has entrusted a third party to manage the relevant common parts and common facilities in the area in question. Huaren Property Company did not provide any management services within that scope. Therefore, Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch should not pay property service fees at the full rate specified in the Preliminary Property Service Contract. c. Taking into account the specific content of the property management services actually provided by Huaren Property Company, the original trial court's discretionary determination that Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch should pay property service fees at 20% of the measured price according to the property fee standard is fair and reasonable and should be affirmed. d. According to the real estate registration information for the 52 houses submitted by Huaren Property Company in the retrial, the total gross floor area of the 52 houses is 16,270.63 square meters. Huaren Property Company calculated the property fee for Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch based on this area in the original trial. The original trial court's calculation of the property fee standard based on the leased area of 18,174.22 square meters as stipulated in the House Lease Contract was erroneous and should be adjusted. (3) Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch did not maliciously breach the contract and should not pay liquidated damages to Huaren Property Company. During the performance of the Preliminary Property Service Contract, Huaren Property Company failed to take reasonable measures to prevent further expansion of losses, and bears significant fault. It should bear responsibility for its own losses. Alternatively, even if it is considered that Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch should pay liquidated damages, the rate of liquidated damages stipulated in the Preliminary Property Service Contract is excessively high, significantly exceeding Huaren Property Company's actual losses, and should be reduced. The nature of the liquidated damages collected by Huaren Property Company is actually interest for overdue payment, which should be calculated based on the one-year loan prime rate (LPR) published by the National Interbank Funding Center authorized by the People's Bank of China. Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch submitted Security Requirements for Bank Business Premises, Basic Service Requirements for Bank Business Outlets, photographs of Haiyi Tiancheng Building and related auxiliary facilities and management, and relevant vouchers, in support of its above claims.

Haiyi Company submitted a written defense stating that when it purchased the property in question, it expressly refused to accept the content of the Preliminary Property Service Contract. That contract no longer applies to the scope of Haiyi Company's purchase, and Haiyi Company designates its own property management and services for the property and auxiliary facilities within the purchased scope. Haiyi Company purchased 52 houses in the community in question, which together constitute all of Floors 1-6 and are objectively separated from other towers. They are all commercial or retail properties in the community. No agreement was reached between Haiyi Company and Huaren Property Company regarding the content and fee standard of property management services, nor are there any relevant agreements on property services. Haiyi Company requested that, on the basis of a comprehensive finding of the facts of the case, all of Huaren Property Company's claims be dismissed.

Huaren Property Company filed a claim with the court of first instance, requesting: 1. An order directing Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company to pay the overdue comprehensive property service fees of RMB 6,883,546.49 (for the period from August 1, 2017 to June 30, 2019); 2. An order directing Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company to pay liquidated damages from the date when the property service fees were due under the contract until the actual date of payment (temporarily calculated as RMB 7,212,460.30 as of June 30, 2019).

The court of first instance found the following facts: On September 6, 2013, Huanhai Company entered into the Preliminary Property Service Contract with Qingdao Huaren Property Management Co., Ltd., selecting Qingdao Huaren Property Management Co., Ltd. to provide preliminary property management services for the Haiyi Tiancheng project. On October 14, 2014, Qingdao Huaren Property Management Co., Ltd. changed its name to Qingdao Huaren Property Co., Ltd. From January 21 to 24, 2015, Haiyi Company entered into 52 Qingdao Commercial Housing Pre-sale Contracts with Huanhai Company, purchasing 52 houses located in the commercial podium of Haiyi Company, Zone G, Floors 1-5, Zone H, and Zone S, Floors 1-6, at No. 29 Donghai West Road, Shinan District, Qingdao. Article 24 of the contracts states: "Party A has selected Qingdao Huaren Property Company to provide preliminary property management for the house and has signed the Preliminary Property Management Service Contract (see Appendix 5) with it. Because the house is planned for commercial use, both parties have signed the Interim Management Rules for Property Owners (see Appendix 5)." Article 11 of the Supplementary Terms of the Contracts, concerning property management, states: "1. Party B confirms that Party A has made Party A aware of the Preliminary Property Service Contract and the Interim Management Rules for Property Owners. Party B agrees that the preliminary property management company designated by Party A shall provide management and services for areas other than those purchased by Party B. 2. Party A agrees that Party B, when using the house, has the right to designate a property service enterprise to manage and service the property and auxiliary facilities within Party B's purchased scope. Party A shall not delay delivery or the issuance of the real estate certificate on this ground. Appendix 5 agreed in the main contract shall no longer be implemented; both parties shall perform in accordance with this clause. 3. Property service fees and elevator operation fees shall be calculated based on the gross floor area. 4. When Party B uses the house, which is planned for commercial (office) use, to carry out business activities, it must comply with Party A's overall commercial (office) plan." On January 21, 2015, Haiyi Company entered into a Power of Attorney with Qingdao Runfeng Jinshi Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Runfeng Company), authorizing Runfeng Company to conduct leasing matters on behalf of Haiyi Company concerning the commercial podium of the Haiyi Tiancheng project, Zones G, H, and S, at No. 29 Donghai West Road, Shinan District, Qingdao. On February 11, 2015, Runfeng Company entered into a House Lease Contract with Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch, providing that the commercial premises located at No. 29 Donghai West Road, Shinan District, Qingdao, Zone G, Floors 1-5, Zone H and Zone S, Floors 1, 2, 5, and 6, with an area of 15,719 square meters, shall be leased to Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch for use, with a lease term from April 1, 2015 to December 31, 2025. On September 29, 2017, Runfeng Company entered into a Supplementary Agreement (I) with Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch, providing that the commercial premises located at No. 29 Donghai West Road, Shinan District, Qingdao, Zone S, Floors 3 and 4, and auxiliary sites, shall be leased to Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch for use, with a lease term from June 15, 2017 to June 14, 2027.

After the delivery of the Haiyi Tiancheng project property, Huaren Property Company provided relevant property management services. Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch leased the houses from Haiyi Company and moved in in July 2015. For the relevant areas of the houses in question, it took responsibility for or procured property services from other entities for daily security, cleaning, and the maintenance of auxiliary facilities and equipment such as water supply, power supply, fire protection, and elevators. In January 2019, Huaren Property Company issued a payment reminder letter and a lawyer's letter to Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch, demanding payment of property service fees and liquidated damages for overdue payment. A dispute arose between Huaren Property Company and Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company over the payment of property service fees, leading to the filing of this lawsuit.

The court of first instance held that this case is a dispute over a property service contract. The issues in this case are: (1) Whether the preliminary property service contract entered into between Huaren Property Company and Huanhai Company is legally binding on Haiyi Company and Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch. (2) Whether Haiyi Company and Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch should pay property service fees and liquidated damages to Huaren Property Company.

(1) Regarding whether the preliminary property service contract in question is legally binding on Haiyi Company and Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch. The establishment of a civil contract relationship presupposes that the parties have reached a meeting of minds. Generally, a civil contract is only legally binding on the parties to the contract. Article 1 of the Property Service Judicial Interpretation provides: "A preliminary property service contract lawfully concluded by the construction unit with a property service enterprise, and a property service contract lawfully concluded by the owners' committee and the general meeting of owners with a property service enterprise selected in accordance with the law, are binding on the property owners. A property owner's defense that he is not a party to the contract shall not be upheld by the people's court." The reason why a preliminary property service contract concluded between the construction unit of a real estate project and a property service enterprise can be legally binding on property owners who are not originally parties to the contract is that, when entering into the property sale and purchase contract, the construction unit made the property owners aware of the relevant content of the preliminary property service contract in accordance with the law and the contract, and the property owners made a clear commitment to accept the preliminary property service contract, or made an implied indication of acceptance of the preliminary property service contract by entering into the property sale and purchase contract. In other words, there is a consensus between the property owners and the construction unit to be bound by the preliminary property service contract.

Article 81 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Property Law") provides: "An owner may manage the building and its auxiliary facilities on his own, or may entrust a property service enterprise or other manager to manage them. With respect to the property service enterprise or other manager engaged by the construction unit, the owner has the right to replace it in accordance with the law." In this case, although Huaren Property Company and Huanhai Company lawfully concluded the preliminary property service contract involved in the case and completed the relevant registration and filing, the commercial housing pre-sale contract concluded between Huanhai Company and Haiyi Company for the 52 units involved in the case expressly provided in Supplementary Clause 11: "1. Party B confirms that Party A has disclosed to Party B the Preliminary Property Service Contract and the Interim Management Regulations for Owners. Party B agrees that the preliminary property management company designated by Party A shall provide management services for the areas other than those purchased by Party B. 2. Party A agrees that Party B shall have the right to designate a property service enterprise to manage and service the property and auxiliary facilities within the scope purchased by Party B when specifically using the premises. Party A shall not delay delivery or delay the issuance of the real estate certificate on this ground. Appendix 5 agreed in the main contract shall no longer be implemented, and the parties shall perform in accordance with this clause." From the content of this supplementary clause, not only did Haiyi Company not make a commitment to accept the constraints of the preliminary property service contract, but it also excluded the application of the preliminary property service contract. With the consent of Huanhai Company, it designated its own property management and services for the property and auxiliary facilities within the purchased scope, only agreeing that the preliminary property management company designated by Huanhai Company, i.e., Huaren Property Company, would provide management services for other areas of the Haiyi Tiancheng project. Accordingly, it can be determined that Haiyi Company did not express an intention to accept the preliminary property service contract involved in the case, and no agreement was reached between Haiyi Company and Huaren Property Company regarding the content of property management services and fee standards for the area and auxiliary facilities involved in the disputed premises. The preliminary property service contract involved in the case cannot automatically have legally binding effect on Haiyi Company.

As a financial institution, the Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch's business premises have certain particularities regarding property management. The 52 units leased by Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch from Haiyi Company are planned for commercial and office use, differing from the residential and hotel apartment use of floors 7 to 44 of the Haiyi Tiancheng project, and are also distinct in terms of area. After moving into the premises involved in the case, Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch either managed the property itself or procured property services from other entities in the name of Haiyi Company or itself. It conducted daily security and cleaning management for these units and the common areas involved, such as corridors, lobbies, stairwells, elevator lobbies, and exterior walls, and performed maintenance and upkeep for auxiliary facilities such as water supply, power supply, elevators, and fire protection equipment. It did not accept management services from Huaren Property Company within the above area. Haiyi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch also did not indicate, through their factual conduct, that they agreed to accept management services from Huaren Property Company for the area and auxiliary facilities involved in the disputed premises.

In summary, Haiyi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch, in both their subjective expression of intent and their factual conduct, did not reach an agreement with Huaren Property Company on the scope, content, fees, and other matters of property services. Huaren Property Company failed to provide effective evidence to prove that Haiyi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch accepted the constraints of the preliminary property service contract involved in the case. The preliminary property service contract involved in the case cannot have legally binding effect on Haiyi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch.

(2) Whether Haiyi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch should pay property service fees to Huaren Property Company. First, since the preliminary property service contract involved in the case has no legally binding effect on Haiyi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch, Huaren Property Company's claim for property service fees and late payment penalties against Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company based on the fee standards stipulated in the preliminary property service contract lacks sufficient basis. Huaren Property Company failed to provide effective evidence to prove that, in accordance with the standards set out in Part 5 (Office Buildings) and Part 6 (Shopping Premises) of the Shandong Provincial Property Service Standards, it provided property services such as building repair and management, common equipment and facility repair and management, order maintenance, emergency handling, fire safety management, cleaning, and greening within the area of the premises purchased by Haiyi Company and leased by Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch. Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company adduced evidence proving that they either managed the services themselves or procured separate property management services. Haiyi Company, Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch, and Huaren Property Company have already entered into a separate agreement on the use of parking spaces, stipulating the content of Huaren Property Company's management services and the relevant fee standards. Huaren Property Company's management of vehicle access and parking in the Haiyi Company residential complex should not give rise to a separate claim for property service fees against the owner and property user.

Second, the actual on-site conditions of the Haiyi Tiancheng project and the evidence provided by Huaren Property Company objectively reflect that Huaren Property Company provided daily management services such as security, cleaning, and greening for the premises and other common areas of the Haiyi Tiancheng project. The master control section of the water, electricity, fire protection, sewage, and other systems of the Haiyi Tiancheng project was also managed and maintained by Huaren Property Company. This master control system is collectively owned by all owners of the Haiyi Tiancheng project and cannot be separated from the water, electricity, fire protection, sewage, and other facilities in the area of the premises leased by Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch from Haiyi Company. Haiyi Company, as the owner, and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch, as the actual user of the property, benefited from the portion of property management services provided by Huaren Property Company. In accordance with the principles of fairness and equivalent compensation, they should pay corresponding property service fees to Huaren Property Company.

Since the preliminary property service contract involved in the case has no legally binding effect on Haiyi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch, the fee standards stipulated in that contract cannot be used to calculate the property service fees payable by Haiyi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch. Huaren Property Company failed to adduce evidence to prove the specific amounts incurred for providing daily management services for the premises of the Haiyi Tiancheng project and for repairing and maintaining the master control section of the water, electricity, fire protection, sewage, and other systems. The technical documents for Huaren Property Company's property management service plan for the Haiyi Tiancheng project, the cost unit prices stated in the detailed calculation of comprehensive property service fees for the Haiyi Tiancheng project, and the measured market prices of property fee fee standards stated in the analysis of property management fee income and expenses all indicated a rate of RMB 13.29 per square meter per month for commercial premises on floors 1 to 2 and office buildings on floors 3 to 6. The preliminary property service contract involved in the case, the technical documents for Huaren Property Company's property management service plan for the Haiyi Tiancheng project, and the relevant provisions of Part 5 (Office Buildings) and Part 6 (Shopping Premises) of the Shandong Provincial Property Service Standards all state that the property services provided by the property service enterprise to the owners include multiple items. Based on the content of the management services actually accepted by Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company from Huaren Property Company, the first instance court found it appropriate to calculate the property service fees for the portion of management services actually provided by Huaren Property Company at 20% of the rate of RMB 13.29 per square meter per month. The total building area of the premises leased by Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch from Haiyi Company is 18,174.22 square meters. For the period from August 1, 2017 to June 30, 2019, the property service fees payable to Huaren Property Company are RMB 13.29 per square meter per month x 20% x 18,174.22 square meters x 23 months = RMB 1,111,063. In the lease contract and supplementary agreement between Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company, it was agreed that Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch would pay for water, electricity, property, and related expenses. Therefore, as the property user, Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch should pay the above property service fees of RMB 1,111,063 to Huaren Property Company, and Haiyi Company, as the owner, shall bear joint and several liability for payment. The first instance court did not support the other parts of the property service fees and liquidated damages claimed by Huaren Property Company in its lawsuit.

In accordance with Article 6 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 72 and 81 of the Property Law, Articles 7, 27, 41, and 42(1) of the Property Management Regulations, Article 7 of the Judicial Interpretation on Property Service Disputes, and Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the first instance court rendered the following judgment: 1. Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch shall pay to Huaren Property Company property service fees of RMB 1,111,063 for the period from August 1, 2017 to June 30, 2019 within ten days from the effective date of this judgment; 2. Haiyi Company shall bear joint and several liability to Huaren Property Company for the property service fees determined in item 1 of this judgment; 3. The other claims of Huaren Property Company are dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 106,376.04 is to be borne by Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company in the amount of RMB 8,382.43, and by Huaren Property Company in the amount of RMB 97,993.61.

Huaren Property Company, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed, requesting: 1. To set aside the first instance judgment and instead order Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company to pay Huaren Property Company the overdue comprehensive property service fees of RMB 6,883,546.49 (from August 1, 2017 to June 30, 2019) and liquidated damages accruing from the date the property service fees were payable as stipulated in the contract until the date of actual payment. 2. The litigation costs of this case to be borne by Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company.

Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed, requesting: 1. To set aside item 1 of the first instance judgment in accordance with the law and instead rule that Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch is not required to pay property service fees and dismiss Huaren Property Company's claims; 2. The litigation costs of both instances to be borne by Huaren Property Company.

The second instance court confirmed the facts found by the first instance court.

The second instance court held that although Huaren Property Company and Huanhai Company concluded the preliminary property service contract involved in the case and completed registration and filing, the commercial housing pre-sale contract between Huanhai Company and Haiyi Company expressly stipulated that the preliminary property service contract would no longer apply to the scope of Haiyi Company's purchase, and Haiyi Company would designate its own property management and services for the property and auxiliary facilities within the purchased scope. Haiyi Company and Huaren Property Company never negotiated on matters such as the content of property management services and fee standards, and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch did not accept management services from Huaren Property Company within the area of the disputed premises. Therefore, the first instance court's determination that the preliminary property service contract involved in the case cannot have legally binding effect on Haiyi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch was factually and legally sound. Since Huaren Property Company could not prove that it provided property services such as building repair and management, common equipment and facility repair and management, order maintenance, emergency handling, fire safety management, cleaning, and greening within the area of the premises purchased by Haiyi Company and leased by Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch in accordance with the relevant standards of the Shandong Provincial Property Service Standards, and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch also submitted evidence proving that it managed the services itself or procured separate property management services, and as previously stated, the preliminary property service contract involved in the case has no legally binding effect on Haiyi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch, the first instance court correctly dismissed Huaren Property Company's claims for property service fees and late payment penalties against Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company based on the fee standards stipulated in the preliminary property service contract. Since Huaren Property Company provided daily management services for the premises and other common areas of the Haiyi Tiancheng project, and the master control section of the water, electricity, fire protection, sewage, and other systems of the Haiyi Tiancheng project was also managed and maintained by Huaren Property Company, and the relevant facilities cannot be separated, Haiyi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch should pay Huaren Property Company the property service fees for this portion. Since Huaren Property Company could not prove the specific amounts actually incurred, the first instance court's finding to calculate the property service fees for the portion of management services actually provided by Huaren Property Company at 20% of the measured market price of the property fee standard of RMB 13.29 per square meter per month was fair and reasonable, and the second instance court should uphold it.

In summary, the appeal requests of both Huaren Property Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch were without merit and should be dismissed. The first instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be upheld.

This Court holds in the retrial that the issues in dispute in this case are: first, whether the "Preliminary Property Service Contract" entered into between Huaren Property Company and Huanhai Company is legally binding on Haiyi Company; second, whether Haiyi Company and Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch should pay property service fees and liquidated damages to Huaren Property Company, and if so, how the amount should be determined.

I. Whether the "Preliminary Property Service Contract" involved in the case is legally binding on Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch and Haiyi Company.

An owner is bound by a preliminary property service contract lawfully entered into between the construction unit and the property service provider, not based on an agreement between the owner and the construction unit to be bound by the preliminary contract, but directly by law. Before the preliminary property service contract is lawfully terminated, it is legally binding on the owner. The court of first instance held that the pre-sale contract for commercial housing stipulated that the preliminary property contract would no longer apply to the purchased scope, that the owner would independently designate property management and services for the purchased property and ancillary facilities, that the owner and the property service company had never negotiated on the content of property management services and fee standards, and that the owner had not received property management services within the area involved in the disputed premises, thereby determining that the preliminary property contract involved could not produce legal binding effect on the owner. This constituted an error in the application of law. Judging from the outcomes of the first and second instance judgments, the conflict between the owner and the property service provider has persisted for a long time, and the case has not achieved a final resolution. Specifically:

1. The legal binding effect of a lawful and effective preliminary property service contract on the owner stems from statutory law. According to the "Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Temporal Effect of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China," this case should apply the former "Property Law," the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," and the "Judicial Interpretation on Property Services," etc. Article 1 of that interpretation provided: "A preliminary property service contract entered into by a construction unit with a property service provider in accordance with the law, and a property service contract entered into by the owners' committee with a property service provider lawfully selected by the owners' assembly, are binding on the owners. If an owner argues on the ground that he is not a party to the contract, the people's court shall not support it." Where a construction unit lawfully enters into a preliminary property service contract with a property service provider, the contract is legally binding on the owner before it is lawfully terminated. Furthermore, Article 24 of the "Regulations on Property Management" provides: "The sales contract entered into between the construction unit and the property buyer shall include the content agreed in the preliminary property service contract." This means that the construction unit and the property buyer reach consensus not only on the property sales contract but also on the statutory generalized assignment of the preliminary property service contract relationship. When the exclusive ownership of a condominium building is transferred between the construction unit and the owner, the preliminary property service contract relationship lawfully entered into by the construction unit is also transferred accordingly by operation of law. In this case, the construction unit Huanhai Company lawfully entered into the "Preliminary Property Service Contract" with Huaren Property Company, selecting Huaren Property Company to provide preliminary property management services for the Haiyi Tiancheng project. The "Preliminary Property Service Contract" is a lawful and effective preliminary property service contract that was concluded and filed in accordance with the statutory procedures within the property management area of the Haiyi Tiancheng project. Haiyi Company purchased the 52 units involved and became an owner within the management area of Huaren Property Company, naturally succeeding to the preliminary property service contract relationship generally and is bound by the "Preliminary Property Service Contract." The preliminary property service contract involved is legally binding on Haiyi Company.

2. The direct legal binding effect of a preliminary property service contract lawfully entered into by the construction unit on the owner ultimately aims to protect the common interests of all owners in condominium buildings. The content of a property service contract includes management and maintenance of common areas and ancillary facilities of the building, greening and maintenance, cleaning and sanitation, maintenance of public order, etc. These services involve the common parts and common interests of all owners. If individual owners were allowed to freely exclude the binding effect of the preliminary property service contract upon purchasing property, refuse to accept the property service provider's management services, and refuse to pay the apportioned property fees, it would make it difficult for the property service provider to sustain the quality of management services provided to the remaining owners, ultimately harming the common interests of all owners. Article 72, Paragraph 1 of the former "Property Law" provides: "Owners have rights and assume obligations with respect to the common parts of the building other than the exclusive parts; they may not refuse to perform obligations on the ground that they have waived their rights." The obligations of a common owner include using the common parts in accordance with their intended use, bearing the costs of daily maintenance and renewal of common parts and public facilities of the land or building, and bearing common management expenses, etc. As common owners, owners should bear the maintenance and management costs of the common parts of the building in order to better exercise exclusive rights and protect the common interests of all owners.

3. Enclosed spaces generally do not constitute a ground for excluding property services. Regarding the independence of the purchased or leased area, Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch claimed that Haiyi Company is the sole owner of the podium (excluding the sixth-floor clubhouse). Haiyi Company responded in its written defense that Haiyi Company purchased 52 units in the community, which together constitute all of floors 1-6 and are objectively independent from the other towers, and requested rejection of all of Huaren Property Company's claims. These arguments cannot stand. (1) Based on the statutory principle of a single property service provider within a specific property management area. The division of property management areas considers factors such as common facilities and equipment, building scale, and community construction. Article 34 of the "Regulations on Property Management" provides that one property management area shall be served by one property service enterprise. Accordingly, the property management area of the community involved should also be served by one property service enterprise, namely Huaren Property Company. The "Preliminary Property Service Contract" clearly specifies the scope of property services, and there is no dispute among the parties that the real estate owned by Haiyi Company and leased by Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch is located within the planning and construction scope of the Haiyi Tiancheng project at No. 29 Donghai West Road, Shinan District, Qingdao, developed by Huanhai Company. According to the facts found in the original trial, the actual conditions of the Haiyi Tiancheng project site and the evidence provided by Huaren Property Company objectively reflect that Huaren Property Company provided daily management services such as security, cleaning, and greening for the Haiyi Tiancheng project compound and other public areas. The master control parts of the water, electricity, fire protection, and sewage systems of the Haiyi Tiancheng project were also managed and maintained by Huaren Property Company, and these master control systems are jointly owned by all owners of the Haiyi Tiancheng project and cannot be separated from the water, electricity, fire protection, and sewage facilities in the area of the property leased by Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch from Haiyi Company. Even if Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch installed access control in the leased area, it still benefited from the property services provided by the property service provider for the maintenance and repair of the building and its public ancillary facilities, the management of community sanitation and environment, and the maintenance of order. (2) Based on the overall consideration of community construction. Even if the building blocks within a community are relatively independent, or there are conditions to create enclosed spaces within a certain range, factors such as the community environment, community construction, and centralized maintenance and management of public facilities like water, electricity, fire protection, and sewage suggest that it is not appropriate for each to act independently and carry out multiple property management services. (3) Based on the need for risk prevention and control. From the evidence submitted by both parties in the litigation, it can be seen that there is a separation and disconnect between the fire master control and terminal maintenance of the community's property. If a fire hazard or disaster occurs, there may be poor coordination in disaster relief, posing certain safety risks and potentially endangering public safety. Evasion of responsibility in such situations would also be detrimental to the protection of rights. (4) Based on the need for harmonious coexistence in social life. Due to Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch's failure to pay property fees while commissioning others to provide services, it stated in the litigation that the parties have had many instances of disharmony in property use and social life, such as garbage disposal, parking, and business operations, with conflicts even escalating to the point of calling the police. (5) Based on the adjudication rules from similar case searches. The legal relationship in Judgment No. 151 is similar to this case, and its adjudication rules may be referenced. That judgment held: Regarding the owner's assertion that it has purchased the entire building, and that the building and its planned land area are exclusively owned by the owner and no longer fall within the scope of property management services as stipulated in the law and the "Preliminary Property Service Contract," the property services provided by the property company are for the public parts of the property, not the exclusive parts within the building. … The owner also failed to prove that the property company had failed to perform or incompletely performed its obligations under the "Preliminary Property Service Contract." Therefore, the owner and the property user should pay property fees in accordance with the standards agreed in the "Preliminary Property Service Contract." That is, even if the owner in the similar case purchased an entire building, it could not exclude the binding effect of the property service contract.

4. The special nature of an owner's industry generally does not constitute a ground for excluding property services. Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch responded in the retrial that its entrustment of a third party to manage the property in the area in question was based on special requirements for the supervision of business premises of financial institutions in the banking industry, not an intentional refusal to accept property management services from Huaren Property Company. It submitted materials such as the "Security Protection Requirements for Bank Business Premises," "Basic Requirements for Bank Business Outlet Services," and the "Security Service Outsourcing Contract." In fact, every industry has its particularities, involving property custody, trade secrets, privacy protection, or professional barriers. However, these particularities should generally be realized within the exclusive parts of the owner's building; for example, large amounts of cash certainly cannot be left in public areas for long periods. Property services include the management and maintenance of buildings and their ancillary facilities in the property service area, maintaining basic order in the property service area, and taking reasonable measures to protect the personal and property safety of owners. From the evidence submitted by Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch and the main costs it bore, these primarily focused on cleaning, garbage disposal, exterior wall cleaning, maintenance and repair of building fire protection facilities, and security service outsourcing. (1) The "Security Protection Requirements for Bank Business Premises," "Basic Requirements for Bank Business Outlet Services," and internal bank regulations are not laws or administrative regulations and cannot conflict with the law. (2) The "Security Protection Requirements for Bank Business Premises" and "Basic Requirements for Bank Business Outlet Services" do not contain special requirements regarding the qualifications of property service providers for bank business outlets, nor do they restrict property service providers from managing and maintaining common property in the public areas of bank business outlets. Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch paid cleaning fees to Qingdao Duomeijie Environmental Engineering Co., Ltd. under the "Cleaning Procurement Contract," entered into a domestic garbage removal contract with a third party, Qingdao Jieyi Billion Clean Co., Ltd., and paid building fire protection facility maintenance and repair fees to Qingdao Venus Technology Engineering Co., Ltd. under the "Building Fire Protection Facility Maintenance and Repair Contract." However, Hengfeng Bank Qingdao Branch did not explain why the above cleaning companies and technology companies met the special security requirements of the bank while Huaren Property Company did not, nor did it explain whether the scope and prices of those service procurement contracts included the exclusive parts of the building. (3) Regarding security services, the primary obligation of the property service provider is to maintain basic order within the property service area and take reasonable measures to protect the personal and property safety of owners. In contrast, commercial institutions like banks procure security outsourcing services primarily based on the legal obligation of managers of public places such as hotels, shopping malls, banks, stations, entertainment venues, or organizers of mass activities to bear tort liability if they fail to fulfill their safety protection obligations and cause harm to others. The two are not equivalent. Security within the property service area cannot replace the bank's security system, and the bank's separate procurement of security services is not a reasonable ground for excluding property services or refusing to pay property fees.

5. The agreement between the developer and the owner in the commercial housing pre-sale contract cannot bind the property service provider. First, the state encourages the developer to select and appoint a property service enterprise with corresponding qualifications through bidding in accordance with the principle of separating real estate development from property management. In this regard, Hua Ren Property Company submitted to the court of first instance the "Registration Form for Bidding and Awarding of Preliminary Property Service Contracts in Qingdao" and reasonably explained that the original was kept with the relevant administrative functional department in Shinan District, Qingdao. Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch and Hai Yi Company, during cross-examination, claimed they could not confirm the authenticity and legality of the evidence but did not submit effective rebuttal evidence. The court of first instance confirmed the authenticity of the evidence. The court of first instance obtained the preliminary property service contract for Hai Yi Tian Cheng from the Urban Management Bureau of Shinan District, Qingdao. The above evidence indicates that the signing of the preliminary property service contract in question went through bidding and was filed with the administrative functional department. Against this background, in 2015, Hai Yi Company and Huan Hai Company signed the "Qingdao Commercial Housing Pre-sale Contract," stipulating: "Party A has selected and appointed Qingdao Hua Ren Property Company to provide preliminary property management for this property and has signed a 'Preliminary Property Management Service Contract' (see Appendix 5) with it. Because the planned use of this property is commercial premises, both Party A and Party B have signed the 'Temporary Management规约 for Owners (see Appendix 5)." Article 11 of the supplementary terms of the contract, concerning property management, states: "1. Party B confirms that Party A has presented to Party B the 'Preliminary Property Service Contract' and the 'Temporary Management规约 for Owners.' Party B agrees that the preliminary property management company designated by Party A shall manage and provide services for areas other than those purchased by Party B. 2. Party A agrees that Party B has the right, when specifically using the property, to designate a property service enterprise to manage and provide services for the property and ancillary facilities within the scope purchased by Party B. Party A cannot use this as a reason to delay delivery or delay the issuance of the property title certificate. Appendix 5 as agreed in the main contract shall no longer be executed; both parties shall perform in accordance with this clause. 3. Property service fees and elevator operation fees shall be calculated based on the building area. 4. When Party B uses the property with a planned use of commercial premises (office) to carry out business activities, it must comply with Party A's overall commercial (office) plan." Regarding the above provisions, Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch and Huan Hai Company stated during the litigation that Hai Yi Company and the developer had agreed in the "Qingdao Commercial Housing Pre-sale Contract" to exclude Hua Ren Property Company from providing property services to the area purchased by Hai Yi Company, and that Hai Yi Company had explicitly refused to accept the content of the "Preliminary Property Service Contract" when purchasing the property in question. That is, it is inappropriate for the developer and the owner, knowing the existence of the preliminary property service contract, to intend to exclude Hua Ren Property Company's rights under the preliminary property service contract in the commercial housing pre-sale contract. The developer, as the signatory of the preliminary property service contract, who also agreed in the commercial housing pre-sale contract that the buyer has the right to designate a property service enterprise to manage and provide services for the property and ancillary facilities within the scope of purchase, violates the principle of good faith. Supporting such conduct would render meaningless the system of selecting and appointing property service enterprises with corresponding qualifications through bidding. Second, based on case law retrieval, Judgment No. 151 held that: Where the developer and the property service company have signed a "Preliminary Property Service Contract," and that contract does not have any statutory circumstances rendering it void, voidable, or discharged, it shall be binding on the owner during the term agreed in the contract. When signing the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract," the developer informed (the owner) of matters such as the fact that it had signed the "Preliminary Property Service Contract" with the property company. Therefore, the owner's defense that it is not a party to the "Preliminary Property Service Contract" and that it has a separate agreement with the developer to pay property fees at a different standard lacks legal basis and is not supported. That is, the judgment held that a separate agreement between the owner and the developer in the "Commercial Housing Sales Contract" cannot exclude the binding effect of a legally valid "Preliminary Property Service Contract" on the owner. Third, Hua Ren Property Company did not participate in the signing of the commercial housing pre-sale contract and did not subsequently ratify the above clauses. It opposed them during the litigation. Under the principle of privity of contract, the above clauses cannot bind Hua Ren Property Company. An agreement between an individual owner and the developer to exclude the application of the preliminary property service contract cannot oppose the preliminary property service contract; the owner remains bound by the preliminary property service contract. Fourth, an individual owner cannot dismiss or appoint a property service provider. Paragraph 2 of Article 81 of the former Property Law provides: "With respect to the property service enterprise or other manager appointed by the developer, the owner has the right to replace it according to law." This provision gives the owner the right to replace the property service provider according to law, but it is also subject to adjustment by Article 76 of the same Law, which provides: "The following matters shall be decided jointly by the owners: ... (4) selecting and appointing and dismissing property service enterprises or other managers; ... Decisions on matters specified in items (5) and (6) of the preceding paragraph shall be made by owners representing two-thirds or more of the total building area and two-thirds or more of the total number of owners." Decisions on other matters specified in the preceding paragraph shall be made by owners representing more than half of the total building area and more than half of the total number of owners. According to the above legal provisions, individual owners such as Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch, by procuring outsourcing services such as cleaning on their own, cannot achieve the legal effect of appointing a new property service provider or dismissing the property service provider under the preliminary property service contract.

II. Regarding the issue of Hai Yi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch paying property service fees and liquidated damages to Hua Ren Property Company

(A) Regarding the issue of the party obligated to pay property service fees

Hai Yi Company has purchased the 52 properties in question, becoming an owner within the management area of Hua Ren Property Company, and is bound by the "Preliminary Property Service Contract." It shall perform its contractual obligations and bear the obligation to pay property service fees to Hua Ren Property Company. Pursuant to Article 7 of the "Judicial Interpretation on Property Service Disputes," where the owner and the lessee, borrower, or other user of the property agree that the property user shall pay the property fee, and the property service enterprise requests that the owner bear joint and several liability, the people's court shall support it. Hai Yi Company submitted the "House Lease Contract" and the "Supplementary Agreement" as evidence during the first instance. Article 5 of the lease contract and Article 4 of the supplementary agreement both clearly stipulate that Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch shall pay water, electricity, property fees, and related expenses in a timely manner as required. Hai Yi Company shall bear joint and several liability for the debt of Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch to pay property service fees under the "Preliminary Property Service Contract."

(B) Regarding the issue of the amount of property service fees payable

A preliminary property service contract signed by the developer and the property service enterprise according to law, and a property service contract signed by the owners' committee and the property service enterprise appointed by the owners' assembly according to law, are binding on the owners. Where an owner argues that it is not a party to the contract, the people's court shall not support it. However, there are still differences between a preliminary property service contract signed by the developer and the property service enterprise and a property service contract signed by the owners' committee and the property service enterprise appointed by the owners' assembly according to law, in terms of the parties signing the contract, the competitiveness and openness of price negotiation, public perception, acceptance by owners, and contract termination. There is room for further improvement of the preliminary property service contract system. Therefore, while recognizing the binding effect of the preliminary property service contract on owners, considering that under the law, the termination of the preliminary property service contract depends on the effectiveness of a property service contract signed by the owners' committee or the owners' assembly with a new property service enterprise, and the difficulty of convening an owners' assembly and establishing an owners' committee leads to difficulties in appointing and dismissing property service providers, the preliminary property service contract may become a de facto perpetual contract. Since individual owners and groups of owners have no opportunity to participate in the negotiation of the preliminary property service contract, strictly adhering to the unit price in the contract may lead to an imbalance of interests. Therefore, the calculation of property fees in this case should be based on the amount calculated according to the property fee standard in the preliminary property service contract, and be handled by considering multiple factors comprehensively.

Article 11, Item 3 of the supplementary terms to the "Qingdao Commercial Housing Pre-sale Contract" clearly stipulates: "Property service fees and elevator operation fees shall be calculated based on the building area." Chapter 3 of the "Hai Yi Company Preliminary Property Service Contract" stipulates property service management fees, divided into seven items, among which the charging standard for property service fees is: "Building 1, Floors 7-44 (high-end residential): RMB 8/month per square meter of building area; Building 2, Floors 7-44 (apartment hotel): RMB 8/month per square meter of building area; Floors 1-2, retail shops: RMB 21/month per square meter of building area; Floors 3-6, office buildings: RMB 17/month per square meter of building area (including secondary water supply operation fees)." As mentioned above, Hai Yi Company is bound by the "Preliminary Property Service Contract" and, in principle, the property fees should be calculated according to the charging standards stipulated in the contract. According to the facts found by the court of first instance, the 52 properties purchased by Hai Yi Company are located in the podium of Floors 1 to 6 of the complex in question, making them owners of the podium Floors 1 to 6 (excluding the clubhouse), which belong to the commercial and office area. The building area of the retail shops on Floors 1-2 is 5,670.98 square meters, and the building area of the office buildings on Floors 3-6 is 10,727.58 square meters, with a total commercial and office building area of 16,398.56 square meters. However, according to the real estate registration information for the 52 properties submitted by Hua Ren Property Company during the retrial, the total building area of the 52 properties is 16,270.63 square meters, of which the building area of the properties on Floors 1-2 is 5,554.70 square meters, and the building area of the office buildings on Floors 3-6 is 10,715.93 square meters. Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch asserted in its retrial response that the total building area of the 52 properties is 16,270.63 square meters, and Hua Ren Property Company also calculated the property fees for Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch in the original trial using this area. Hua Ren Property Company agreed in this court's retrial to calculate the property fees based on the above area data. According to the charging standard stipulated in the contract, the monthly property fee is RMB 298,819.51 (RMB 17/month per square meter of building area × 10,715.93 square meters + RMB 21/month per square meter of building area × 5,554.70 square meters = RMB 298,819.51). For the 23-month period from August 1, 2017, to June 30, 2019, the property fee calculated at the contract unit price totals RMB 6,872,848.73. Based on a comprehensive calculation, the unit price of the preliminary property service contract property fee per month per square meter is RMB 18.37 (RMB 298,819.51 ÷ 16,270.63 = RMB 18.37).

Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch argued in its retrial response that, even if the "Preliminary Property Service Contract" is binding on Hai Yi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch, because Hua Ren Property Company actually provided only part of the property services, the original trial judgment's discretionary determination of the property service fee based on the actual services provided by Hua Ren Property Company was entirely correct and fair. This court holds that this argument cannot stand. Where a property service provider has provided services in accordance with the agreement and relevant regulations, the owner shall not refuse to pay the property fee on the grounds that it has not accepted or does not need to accept the relevant property services. Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch implemented closed management of the premises it leased from Hai Yi Company and the related public areas, and was responsible for managing or procuring services such as security, cleaning, garbage removal, exterior wall cleaning, water supply, power supply, elevator, and fire-fighting equipment maintenance and repair. It cannot refuse to pay the property fee on this ground. Considering that due to the closed management, Hua Ren Property Company could not provide property services such as housing repair and management, shared equipment and facility repair and management, order maintenance, emergency handling, fire safety management, cleaning, and greening in accordance with the standards specified in Part 5 (Office Buildings) and Part 6 (Shopping Malls) of the "Shandong Province Property Service Standards," related costs should have decreased, and the property fee should be appropriately reduced. Meanwhile, based on the arguments and evidence presented by both parties during the litigation, Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch installed access controls on the leased premises for closed management, preventing Hua Ren Property Company from entering the area leased by Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch to provide property services. Therefore, the cost reduction consideration is only a secondary factor in reducing the property fee standard.

Hai Yi Company submitted a written defense arguing that all the commercial premises or shops in the complex in question were involved, that Hai Yi Company and Hua Ren Property Company had not reached any agreement on the content of property management services and charging standards, and that there was no relevant agreement on property services. It requested that, based on a full investigation of the facts of this case, all of Hua Ren Property Company's claims be dismissed. This court holds that: According to the "Measures for the Administration of Property Service Charging" issued by the National Development and Reform Commission and the former Ministry of Construction, property service charging shall distinguish between the nature and characteristics of different properties and implement government-guided prices or market-adjusted prices respectively. For property service charges subject to market-adjusted prices, the owner and the property management enterprise shall agree in the property service contract. From the statements of both parties during the litigation, Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch consistently considered Hua Ren Property Company's property fee standard to be too high, and the parties could not reach an agreement on the charging standard. During the retrial hearing, Hua Ren Property Company could not adequately explain the basis for the property fee pricing in the commercial and office areas in question. After the hearing, it did not sufficiently submit market comparisons of property fees for similar properties at the same period or neighboring properties. In the evaluation report submitted to this court, it only listed Porsche Tower at RMB 17/month per square meter and Wanli Haijing at RMB 10/month per square meter. Even if the above situation is true, the property fee standard in dispute in this case is still high.

In summary, considering that Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch purchased services itself in the leased area, and Hua Ren Property Company accordingly reduced its costs for property services within the area leased by Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch; the fact found in the first instance that Hua Ren Property Company's technical document for the property management service plan for the Hai Yi Tian Cheng project, the cost unit price stated in the detailed calculation of comprehensive property service fees for Hai Yi Tian Cheng, and the measured price of the property fee charging standard stated in the income and expenditure analysis of property management fees were all RMB 13.29/month per square meter for the commercial area on Floors 1-2 and office buildings on Floors 3-6; and factors such as the fee standards of neighboring properties, this court, aiming to facilitate a more stable property service relationship between the parties in the future, takes the property fee under the preliminary property service contract in question as the base and reduces the property fee in this case by 20% on a discretionary basis. The property service fees for the period from August 1, 2017, to June 30, 2019, that Hai Yi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch shall pay to Hua Ren Property Company are RMB 5,498,278.98 (RMB 6,872,848.73 × 80%). Deducting the RMB 1,111,063 paid by Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch after the original judgment, the remaining property service fee payable is RMB 4,387,215.98 (RMB 5,498,278.98 - RMB 1,111,063 = RMB 4,387,215.98).

(III) Regarding the issue of the amount of liquidated damages

Article 114, Paragraph 2 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If the agreed liquidated damages are lower than the losses caused, the people's court or arbitration institution may increase them upon the request of the party. If the agreed liquidated damages are excessively higher than the losses caused, the people's court or arbitration institution may reduce them appropriately upon the request of the party." In this case, according to Article 29 of the "Preliminary Property Service Contract," if an owner fails to pay the property service fee in full and on time, it shall pay liquidated damages at a rate of three-thousandths (0.3%) per day of the amount payable from the date of default. Accordingly, Hua Ren Property Company claimed that Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch and Hai Yi Company should pay liquidated damages from the date the property service fee was due under the contract until the actual date of payment, provisionally calculated as RMB 7,212,460.30 as of June 30, 2019. Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch argued in its retrial response that the liquidated damages standard stipulated in the "Preliminary Property Service Contract" was too high and should be reduced, and should be calculated based on the one-year loan prime rate (LPR) published by the National Interbank Funding Center authorized by the People's Bank of China. This court holds that the liquidated damages standard of three-thousandths per day stipulated in the preliminary property service contract in question is too high. Furthermore, the legal relationship in this case has certain particularities and requires specialized knowledge. Hai Yi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch did not intentionally default for a long period. After the original judgment confirmed that they should pay the property fee, Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch also promptly paid part of the property fee to Hua Ren Property Company. To encourage owners to pay property fees in a timely manner and to prevent future defaults, this court calculates, according to the charging standard stipulated in the contract, the monthly property fee as RMB 298,819.51, and at 80%, it is RMB 239,055.61. The contract provides for monthly payment. Hai Yi Company and Evergrowing Bank Qingdao Branch shall pay liquidated damages to Hua Ren Property Company from the date the property service fee was due until the actual date of payment, calculated based on the benchmark interest rate for loans of the same type and same period published by the People's Bank of China for the period prior to August 19, 2019, and from August 20, 2019, based on the one-year loan prime rate (LPR) published by the National Interbank Funding Center authorized by the People's Bank of China (the portion of the property fee of RMB 1,111,063 that has been paid shall no longer accrue liquidated damages from the date of payment).

In conclusion, the original judgment erred in fact-finding and applied the law incorrectly, and should be corrected according to law. This court, pursuant to Article 214, Paragraph 1 and Article 177, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, hereby orders as follows:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment (2020) Lu Min Zhong No. 2866 of the Shandong High People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2019) Lu 71 Min Chu No. 87 of the Jinan Railway Transport Intermediate People's Court;

2. Evergrowing Bank Co., Ltd. Qingdao Branch shall, within ten days from the date this judgment takes effect, pay to Qingdao Hua Ren Property Co., Ltd. the property service fees for the period from August 1, 2017, to June 30, 2019, in the amount of RMB 4,387,215.98, and pay liquidated damages calculated on the base of a monthly property fee of RMB 239,055.61 from the date the respective monthly property service fee was due until the actual date of payment, calculated based on the benchmark interest rate for loans of the same type and same period published by the People's Bank of China for the period prior to August 19, 2019, and from August 20, 2019, based on the one-year loan prime rate (LPR) published by the National Interbank Funding Center authorized by the People's Bank of China (the portion of the property fee of RMB 1,111,063 that has been paid shall no longer accrue liquidated damages from the date of payment);

3. Qingdao Hai Yi Tian Cheng Commercial Management Co., Ltd. shall bear joint and several liability to Qingdao Hua Ren Property Co., Ltd. for the payment of the property service fees specified in Item 2 of this judgment;

4. Dismiss the other claims of Qingdao Hua Ren Property Co., Ltd.

If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 260 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
